papers.title: Where Planning Changes the Outcome of Orbital Games
papers.summary: This paper introduces OrbitalGym, a simulation environment for studying when planning algorithms or system design determine the outcome of adversarial orbital encounters. In an orbital game, two non-cooperative teams of satellites maneuver during rendezvous and proximity operations to win a differential-reward objective. Advances in terrestrial game playing have prompted many methods for orbital games, but studies typically evaluate one method in one scenario, often against a passive or random defender. It is unclear whether better planning matters once vehicle capability (maneuverability, sensing, communications) and adversarial responses are considered. OrbitalGym is a JAX-based environment supporting varying numbers of agents, state representations (position, velocity, attitude, fuel), explicit or implicit communication, and proximity or conical field-of-view sensors. It compiles games to batched GPU code, enabling large-scale parallel simulation of policies across many configurations. This identifies regimes where policy choice affects outcomes and regimes where system capability dominates. We study two close-range games: pursuit-evasion, where one spacecraft tries to capture another, and lady-bandit-guard, where a guard prevents an attacker from reaching a protected asset. We compare PD, LQR, model predictive path integral control, and Monte Carlo tree search over ratios of thrust and propellant, initial separation, game duration, sensor capability, and the definition of capture. In pursuit-evasion the propellant ratio decides most encounters: against five of six evader policies, pursuer policy changes capture probability by 10 percent or more in at most 15 of 90 capability configurations. In lady-bandit-guard, policy matters more: against bandits able to reach the asset, a better guard policy raises defense probability by at least 10 percent in 56 to 74 of 90 configurations.

papers.title: Adaptive Orbit-Aided Vector Tracking for Orbit Determination of LEO Satellites
papers.summary: Reliable orbit determination for CubeSats is essential for emerging low-Earth-orbit positioning, navigation, and timing (LEO-PNT) applications. However, onboard orbit determination remains constrained by single-frequency GNSS code-based receivers, intermittent signal reception, and highly dynamic orbital conditions. This paper proposes an adaptive orbit-aided vector tracking (OAVT) algorithm for LEO-PNT CubeSat orbit determination under these conditions. The method employs a GNSS vector tracking loop (VTL) as the primary navigation estimator and loosely couples it with a low-fidelity orbital dynamics model (ODM), which provides auxiliary position and velocity pseudo-measurements. The contribution of the ODM is regulated through adaptive covariance assignment based on GNSS stress and the residual consistency between the ODM and GNSS solutions. Under nominal conditions, OAVT preserves the accuracy advantage of VTL over the conventional scalar tracking loop. The 3D position root-mean-square error (RMSE) is reduced from 2.631\,m for STL to 1.081\,m, while the 3D velocity RMSE decreases from 0.3985\,m/s to 0.1023\,m/s. Under degraded conditions, OAVT provides substantially greater robustness than both STL and standalone VTL. The 3D position RMSE remains bounded at 8.27\,m during a complete signal outage, 10.17\,m during gradual signal loss and reacquisition, and 26.65\,m under variable visibility, whereas STL fails to produce valid solutions and standalone VTL loses lock. These results demonstrate that OAVT substantially improves solution robustness and state continuity with only a moderate increase in computational burden, making it suitable for CubeSat orbit determination and future LEO-PNT missions.

papers.title: Anisotropic Trust Region Warping for Prior-Data Fitted Networks in Bayesian Optimisation
papers.summary: Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) replace the hyperparameter refitting of Gaussian Process (GP) surrogates in Bayesian optimisation with a single forward pass, at the cost of a prior that is fixed at meta-training time. We show empirically that a PFN's predictive log-likelihood falls increasingly behind that of a refitted GP as the objective function's lengthscale grows beyond the mode of the PFN's meta-training prior, and that this deficit carries over to optimisation performance. To correct the mismatch without retraining the network, we introduce Anisotropic Trust Region (ATR) warping. Per-dimension lengthscales are estimated by kernel target alignment, and an affine rescaling of the input space maps the objective onto the lengthscale the PFN expects, with a trust region around the anchor determining which observations are retained, leaving the PFN's $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot N^2)$ inference cost unchanged. On functions drawn from a Mat\'ern-3/2 kernel, ATR warping improves optimisation performance of the PFN at both extremes of the lengthscale range. Our implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/youngers2006/Trust-Region-Warping-For-PFNs.

papers.title: Generative modeling for fusion: a large-scale benchmark of stellarator fast-ion simulations
papers.summary: Stellarators offer a promising magnetic confinement approach for achieving controlled nuclear fusion. However, stellarator design remains challenging, as evaluating configuration performance requires computationally expensive, high-fidelity simulations. In particular, key performance metrics derived from guiding center simulations are costly to include directly in the design optimization loop, and are almost exclusively used as diagnostics. Machine learning has the potential to advance fusion research by enabling rapid generation and evaluation of new stellarator configurations. Effectively applying ML for fusion demands large-scale datasets that capture both design diversity and high-fidelity simulation outputs. In this work, we introduce the Benchmark of Stellarator Simulations (BoSS), a dataset of stellarator designs paired with guiding center simulation results and trajectories. The BoSS is the first large-scale dataset of guiding center simulations, containing simulation data for 180,000 distinct magnetohydrodynamic equilibria spanning a wide range of magnetic geometries and confinement properties. To exemplify the utility of ML to accelerate stellarator design, we formulate and address two sets of modeling tasks: generative modeling for designing stellarators with good particle confinement, and surrogate modeling for predicting stellarator heat deposition patterns and particle trajectories. The tasks reveal the potential impact ML can have in the stellarator field and important opportunities to improve the applicability of ML models in the sciences. Our baselines generate diverse, performant stellarators and provide useful surrogate predictions, and point to long-horizon trajectory forecasting and out-of-distribution generation as key directions for future work. The BoSS can be accessed through https://boss.flatironinstitute.org/.

papers.title: Application of PDE emulators for a multi-material, multi-physics simulation problem
papers.summary: Machine learning (ML) architectures are being developed for fast emulation of numerical simulators to accelerate both scientific discovery and engineering design. While these approaches are well-tested on popular PDE (partial differential equation) benchmarks, it is necessary to evaluate their performance on datasets that more accurately reflect industrial and engineering applications. We evaluate several computer vision-based architectures trained as surrogate models on a challenging computational physics task involving multiple materials, revealing significant implementation challenges for adapting certain pre-trained models, including transformer-based architectures. For such multi-physics multi-material datasets, our results underscore the importance of learning algorithms designed for sparse and imbalanced data, techniques for adapting spatial encodings and physical consistency metrics, in addition to methods for reducing the cost of generating sufficient training data.

papers.title: Predicting Sparse Observables in Parameterized Unsteady Flows Using Coarse-Mesh Graph Neural Networks
papers.summary: Full-order surrogates for high-dimensional nonlinear flows are often unnecessary when applications require only selected degrees of freedom. We propose reduced-order models that bypass full-state reconstruction by deploying graph neural networks (GNNs) directly on coarse meshes. Applied to parameterized 2D/3D confined cylinder flows and an unevenly heated cavity over Reynolds/Rayleigh-number ranges, the models generalize to unseen conditions and accurately predict sparse probe locations and integrated quantities. Coarse-mesh GNNs match or outperform finer-mesh surrogates while reducing training time and memory, even for 3D chaotic dynamics. A dynamics-informed adaptive sampling strategy guided by frequency-spectrum variations reduces maximum errors by an order of magnitude versus uniform sampling at negligible cost. Coarse-mesh training also makes noise-augmented multi-step unrolling practical, improving long-horizon autoregressive predictions. The approach outperforms parametric DMD, sparse MLPs, U-Nets, and Fourier neural operators at lower cost, and enables system identification and state estimation from sparse observations. These results show that coarse-mesh representations, adaptive sampling, and noise-augmented unrolled training form an efficient framework for reduced-order modeling of parameterized unsteady flows without solver-resolution reconstruction.

papers.title: Efficient Deep Gaussian Process Surrogates via Mini-Batch Latent MAP Estimation
papers.summary: Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) are flexible surrogate models for computer experiments with nonstationary response surfaces, but inference over their latent representations remains computationally challenging. Existing methods typically rely on variational inference or Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), which impose variational-family assumptions or require costly posterior sampling. We propose the latent maximum-a-posteriori deep Gaussian process (LaMP-DGP), which uses gradient-based optimization to obtain MAP estimates of the latent representations and enables efficient probabilistic prediction through linked-GP calculations. To scale LaMP-DGP to large datasets, we develop a mini-batch optimization algorithm and, under a polynomial mini-batch bias-decay condition, establish a stationarity bound for latent-state optimization that motivates a growing batch-size schedule. Across numerical experiments and real-data analyses, LaMP-DGP provides consistently competitive predictive performance relative to doubly stochastic variational inference, stochastic gradient Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, and fully Bayesian Vecchia DGP inference. Computationally, LaMP-DGP is substantially faster than the Vecchia MCMC approach while remaining broadly competitive with the stochastic-gradient alternatives. These results position LaMP-DGP as a competitive and computationally efficient alternative for DGP inference. An R package, "LaMPDGP", is available for implementing the proposed method.

papers.title: In-Context Learning for Multi-Fidelity Multiscale Model Closure and Cross-Operator Out-Of-Distribution Generalization
papers.summary: Multi-fidelity learning uses low-fidelity information (coarse-scale PDE models) together with limited high-fidelity data (fine-scale solutions) to obtain high-accuracy PDE solutions. It is a data-driven approach to downscale reduced-order models to solve PDEs efficiently and accurately. Standard multi-fidelity learning focuses on one operator or PDE; given a new PDE, retraining using additional coarse-fine solution pairs may be required, which is costly. In this work, we propose an in-context multi-fidelity learning framework for learning multiple multi-fidelity operators with one shared model. The model is trained using paired low- and high-fidelity examples as demonstrations from multiple operators, together with a new coarse-scale solution query, to predict the corresponding fine-scale solution. Once trained, given a new PDE operator, a few (fewer than five) coarse-fine demonstration pairs, and a low-cost coarse query, the model predicts the corresponding fine-scale solution without fine-tuning. When the target operator appears in the training dataset but has a different prediction goal, such as predicting beyond the training time interval, no additional demonstrations are needed. Instead, the model uses training coarse-fine pairs from that PDE and information from other training operators. Testing then only requires generating a low-cost coarse-scale solution query, without fine-tuning. Notably, our smallest model contains only 255,364 trainable parameters, corresponding to approximately 456 parameters per training operator for 560 operators.
papers.title_ja: マルチフィデリティ・マルチスケールモデルクローズおよびクロスオペレータの分布外汎化のためのインコンテキスト学習
papers.summary_ja: 低忠実度PDEモデルと高忠実度データを用いたマルチフィデリティ学習において、新しいPDE演算子への適応に高コストな再学習が必要という課題を解決する。本論文は、複数の演算子からなるデモデータとクエリを提示するだけで、ファインチューニングなしに高忠実度解を予測するインコンテキスト学習フレームワークを提案する。これにより、訓練済み演算子であっても予測目標が異なる場合や、未知の演算子であっても少数のデモペアがあれば、低コストな粗解クエリのみで高精度な解を得られる。さらに、わずか25万パラメータという極めて軽量なモデルサイズで、560個の演算子に対する効率的な汎化性能を実現している。

papers.title: A Hybrid Physics-informed holomorphic neural networks Method
papers.summary: Physics-informed holomorphic neural networks (PIHNNs) exploit complex-analytic representations to satisfy homogeneous PDEs by construction, but their extension to nonhomogeneous problems is nontrivial. We propose a hybrid physics-informed holomorphic neural network (HPIHNN) framework based on a decomposition of the solution into particular and homogeneous components. The particular component is computed by a spectral method on a simple extended domain, while the homogeneous component is approximated by a PIHNN trained only on the boundary with modified boundary data. The resulting formulation avoids meshing complex geometries and retains the dimensionality-reduction advantage of holomorphic representations. The method is applied to nonhomogeneous Poisson, Stokes, biharmonic, linear elasticity, and Helmholtz equations. Numerical experiments covering complex geometries, corner singularities, and nearly incompressible regimes demonstrate that the proposed method accurately resolves the corresponding solutions and, in the considered tests, generally achieves lower errors and shorter training times than standard PINNs. The results indicate that coupling spectral particular solutions with holomorphic neural approximations provides an efficient approach to nonhomogeneous PDEs on complex domains.
papers.title_ja: ハイブリッド物理情報ホロモルフィックニューラルネットワーク手法
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、非斉次偏微分方程式（PDE）の解を特定解と斉次解に分解するハイブリッド手法（HPIHNN）を提案する。特定解はスペクトル法で、斉次解は境界条件のみを用いた物理情報ホロモルフィックニューラルネットワーク（PIHNN）で近似することで、複雑な幾何学形状におけるメッシュ生成を回避しつつ次元削減の利点を維持する。ポアソン方程式やストークス方程式などの非斉次問題への適用実験において、標準的なPINNと比較して誤差が低く学習時間が短いことを示した。

papers.title: Robust Active Learning for More Efficient and Reliable Paths to Optimal Design
papers.summary: Simulation-driven design optimization requires active learning strategies that efficiently combine models with different computational costs and levels of fidelity. We introduce Multifidelity Cost-Aware Screening (MF-CAS), which enables the joint selection of sampling location and fidelity using a surrogate that provides decomposed uncertainty intervals rather than a complete predictive probability distribution. MF-CAS exploits the contribution of each fidelity to the high-fidelity uncertainty together with its computational cost to determine whether a candidate should first be evaluated at low fidelity or directly progressed towards high fidelity. The method is assessed on the constrained 14-dimensional hydrodynamic optimization of the DTMB 5415 hull under a deliberately limited computational budget. MF-CAS achieves an approximately 9.0% resistance reduction, compared with 6.7% for the best baseline optimisation method, demonstrating that incorporating fidelity-resolved uncertainty directly into the joint location-fidelity decision can substantially improve multifidelity active learning efficiency.

papers.title: Supervised Fine-Tuning for Reasoning Large Language Models: A Survey
papers.summary: Large reasoning models have recently demonstrated remarkable capabilities in solving complex tasks, where supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on long chain-of-thought data serves as a crucial foundation for eliciting and enhancing their reasoning abilities. Despite rapid progress in both improving and analyzing reasoning-oriented SFT, the field still lacks a systematic survey that consolidates its fast-growing literature. To fill this gap, we present a comprehensive review of recent advancements in reasoning SFT, examining the literature through the dual lenses of methodological design and analytical investigation. First, we review methodological improvements across the SFT pipeline and categorize them into data-centric approaches and algorithm-centric innovations. Second, we reorganize analytical studies along three dimensions: data characteristics, optimization dynamics, and mechanistic insights. Finally, by synthesizing current research focuses and remaining bottlenecks, we outline promising future directions for reasoning SFT. We hope this survey deepens the understanding of reasoning SFT and paves the way for advanced reasoning models.

papers.title: Think Twice: The Metis-1.6 Technical Report
papers.summary: Metis is a bet that better data, better training methods and new architectures can buy what a bigger parameter count cannot, at a fraction of the cost. Metis-1.6 is its latest step: two language models built from scratch by a single researcher, Praxis (2.94B parameters, 0.46B active per pass) and Logos (10.23B parameters, 1.18B active per pass). Both run a hybrid Mamba-2 and attention mixture-of-experts stack twice for every token, so each token gets a second look. Each was trained on 1.02T tokens in total: 804.76B of pretraining, 18B of context extension to 131,072 tokens, and 200B of supervised fine-tuning. Metis-1.6 was never meant to challenge frontier models, and across 40 post-trained benchmarks it mostly does not: Logos averages 52.93, seventh of 17 models in its comparison set and within a point of Qwen3-4B. But it gets there on roughly a twelfth of the median training data of the comparators that disclose it, and with fewer active parameters per token than any model that beats it, which puts it on the Pareto frontier for both. In mathematics it ranks second of 30 models, with 67.50% on AIME 2025 and 63.64% on HMMT February 2026. It is weak at code, instruction following and long context. The rest of the report is the part I found most valuable: what went wrong. The optimizer I configured never ran, and attention trained with AdamW for all of pretraining. A 1.77B-parameter n-gram memory learned to switch itself off. Five fine-tuning choices cost capability. And a length reward under group-mean normalization punished correct solutions for being long once a group's pass rate passed 2/3, a sign inversion I prove and fix with a one-line clamp. I close with the 10B-token ablations behind MoRE (Mixture of Recursive Experts), the looped architecture of Metis-1.7.
papers.title_ja: Think Twice: Metis-1.6 技術レポート
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、Mamba-2 とアテンションを組み合わせるハイブリッド MoE アーキテクチャを採用した LLM「Metis-1.6」の技術詳細を報告する。単一研究者が構築したこのモデルは、比較対象の中央値の約 1/12 の学習データ量で、数学推論において上位 2 位に入る高い効率性を示した。さらに、オプティマイザ設定ミスや長文報酬の符号反転など、訓練過程で発生した具体的な問題点とその修正手法を詳細に分析している。最後に、再帰的エキスパート混合（MoRE）によるループ型アーキテクチャ「Metis-1.7」への拡張についても言及している。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM の効率化・推論高速化・新アーキテクチャ設計に直結する内容

papers.title: FAD-KV: Adaptive Dictionary KV Caching for Efficient Reasoning Decoding
papers.summary: Key-value (KV) caching is a core mechanism in large language models, where intermediate key and value representations are stored to accelerate autoregressive decoding. As generation length increases, KV cache memory and computation grow linearly, making compression critical for efficient long-output reasoning. Dictionary-based sparse KV compression is appealing because it represents each token's KV states as a sparse combination of learned basis elements (atoms) in a dictionary, preserving token-level structure without enforcing a global low-rank constraint. However, existing dictionary-based methods face two practical limitations during decoding: iterative sparse coding methods such as Orthogonal Matching Pursuit add decoding-time overhead, and static dictionaries may mismatch evolving KV distributions under test-time generation. While adaptive dictionary updates can reduce this mismatch, naive append-only strategies lead to dictionary growth during generation. We propose FAD-KV, a \textbf{F}ast \textbf{A}daptive \textbf{D}ictionary KV caching framework for efficient reasoning decoding. FAD-KV integrates (i) a screening-based sparse coding scheme, where a one-shot Top-\(n\) selection identifies a small candidate pool followed by lightweight coefficient refinement, and (ii) a fixed-size dictionary adaptation mechanism that reuses inactive atoms instead of expanding the dictionary. By controlling both sparse coding cost and adaptive dictionary growth, FAD-KV provides a memory-bounded and computation-efficient KV compression framework for long reasoning workloads. Experiments on reasoning and long-context benchmarks show that FAD-KV achieves a strong quality-efficiency trade-off while avoiding unbounded dictionary growth during decoding.
papers.title_ja: FAD-KV: 効率的な推論デコーディングのための適応型辞書KVキャッシュ
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）の推論デコーディングにおけるKVキャッシュのメモリと計算コストを削減する手法「FAD-KV」を提案する。既存の辞書ベースのスパース圧縮法が持つ、反復的なスパースコーディングによる計算オーバーヘッドと、静的辞書による分布ミスマッチ、あるいは辞書の無制限な増大という問題を解決する。スクリーニングベースのスパースコーディングと、非活性アトムを再利用する固定サイズ辞書適応機構を統合し、メモリと計算を効率的に制御する。推論および長文脈ベンチマークにおいて、品質と効率のバランスを維持しつつ、デコーディング中の辞書増大を回避する強力なトレードオフを実現した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論高速化・KVキャッシュ圧縮というユーザーの関心と直接一致

papers.title: SkillMem: Compact External Skill Memory for Latent Multi-Agent Reasoning
papers.summary: Latent multi-agent systems reduce inference cost by keeping intermediate reasoning and inter-agent communication in continuous representations.\ Reusable skills, however, are commonly supplied as text or stored as layer-wise Key-Value states or skill-specific model parameters, introducing repeated processing or substantial per-skill storage.\ We introduce \textbf{SkillMem}, which represents each reusable skill as a small external latent memory and makes it directly available during latent multi-agent reasoning.\ A role-conditioned cross-attention reader allows the same memory to guide different agents according to their roles and current hidden states.\ We train the skill memories and shared reader through behavioral distillation, matching the change in token predictions induced by a textual skill while keeping the backbone frozen.\ For our experiments, we obtain textual skills from paired successful and failed multi-agent trajectories, although existing skills can also be compiled directly.\ Across six benchmarks and Qwen3 models ranging from 4B to 14B parameters, SkillMem provides strong gains for smaller backbones while preserving efficient latent multi-agent inference across model scales.\ We use the same $8\times256$ memory configuration across all evaluated model scales, requiring 9.6\,KB of skill-specific storage per skill, including its retrieval embedding.\ For a library of 100 skills, SkillMem reduces total storage by more than $38\times$ compared with alternative skill representations and achieves up to a $4.23\times$ end-to-end inference speedup.\ These results show that compact procedural memories can be reused without sacrificing the efficiency of latent multi-agent reasoning.
papers.title_ja: SkillMem: 潜在マルチエージェント推論のためのコンパクトな外部スキルメモリ
papers.summary_ja: 潜在マルチエージェントシステムにおける推論コスト削減とスキル再利用の効率化を目的とした手法を提案する。各スキルを小さな外部潜在メモリとして表現し、役割条件付きクロスアテンションリーダーによって異なるエージェントに適用可能にする。バックボーンを凍結したまま行動蒸留により学習し、テキストベースのスキル表現と比較して最大38倍のストレージ削減と4.23倍の推論高速化を実現した。Qwen3モデル（4B〜14B）を用いた6つのベンチマークで、特に小規模モデルにおいて顕著な性能向上を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論高速化・メモリ効率化・エージェント設計の核心に直結

papers.title: Bi-Phase Training: Learning Efficiently From Scratch
papers.summary: Pre-training foundational models is computationally expensive as models scale. In this work, we introduce Bi-Phase Training (BPT), a parameter-efficient pre-training method that preserves the high-rank learning dynamics observed in full-parameter optimization with substantially reduced trainable parameters. BPT parameterizes each weight update as a composition of constrained high-rank left/right transformations via trainable diagonal matrices and low-rank adapters whose updates are periodically merged into the frozen base weights, resulting in a compounding expansion of accessible directions during training. Across language-model pre-training from scratch (Qwen2.5 models from 100M to 1.5B parameters and OLMo-2-1B) on FineWeb-Edu (10B and 100B tokens), BPT achieves validation perplexity close to full-parameter baselines while using far fewer trainable parameters; e.g., at the 1.5B scale, BPT uses 66% fewer trainable parameters with only a small validation-perplexity gap. Additionally, a comprehensive evaluation across diverse downstream tasks shows that BPT preserves much of the full-parameterized model's downstream performance.
papers.title_ja: 二相学習：ゼロから効率的に学習する
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデルの事前学習における計算コスト削減を目的とした、パラメータ効率の高い事前学習手法「Bi-Phase Training (BPT)」を提案する。BPTは、凍結されたベース重みへの低ランクアダプタと対角行列による高ランク変換の合成を通じて、学習可能なパラメータ数を大幅に削減しながら、フルパラメータ最適化と同様の高ランク学習ダイナミクスを維持する。Qwen2.5やOLMo-2-1Bなどのモデルを用いた実験では、学習可能パラメータを66%削減しても検証パープレキシティの劣化は最小限にとどまり、下流タスクでの性能もフルパラメータモデルに匹敵することが示された。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの事前学習効率化とパラメータ削減が直接関心領域に該当するため

papers.title: Efficient Joint Trajectory Optimization and Resource Allocation for Secure UAV Networks: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.summary: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly deployed in wireless networks; however, ensuring secure communication and efficient energy usage remains challenging. This paper addresses the joint trajectory optimization and resource allocation problem in UAV networks in the presence of a tethered UAV flying center and a malicious ground eavesdropper. In the proposed model, UAVs are equipped with energy harvesting capabilities and can adaptively switch between transmitting, jamming, and relaying roles to deliver data to a tethered UAV center for optimized network performance. An optimization problem is formulated to maximize a utility function that balances secrecy rate, energy consumption, and interference. To address the high non-convexity of the problem and its real-time decision requirements, a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithm is proposed to solve the problem and learn the network dynamics. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior secrecy performance, lower energy consumption, and reduced interference compared to conventional and DRL-based methods.
papers.title_ja: 安全なUAVネットワークにおける効率的な軌道最適化とリソース割当：深層強化学習アプローチ
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、UAVネットワークにおける通信セキュリティとエネルギー効率を両立させるための軌道最適化とリソース割当問題を扱う。エネルギーハーベスティング機能を備えたUAVが、送信・ジャミング・中継の役割を適応的に切り替えるモデルを提案し、秘密率とエネルギー消費のバランスを最大化する非凸最適化問題を定式化する。この複雑な問題のリアルタイム解決のため、近接方策最適化（PPO）に基づく深層強化学習アルゴリズムを適用し、ネットワークダイナミクスを学習させる。シミュレーション結果により、従来の手法や既存のDRL手法と比較して、優れた秘密性能、低いエネルギー消費、および干渉低減効果が示された。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習による軌道最適化とリソース割当の統合が関心に直結

papers.title: Trajectory-Planning Attitude Control System for Satellites with Magnetic Attitude Control and One Reaction Wheel
papers.summary: Selecting attitude actuators for spacecraft in low earth orbit (LEO) often involves a trade between reaction wheels and magnetorquers. Reaction wheels generally have higher size, weight and power as well as cost, compared with magnetorquers, but have performance advantages. We consider a hybrid system relying on a single reaction wheel and three magnetorquers, using a trajectory planning control method that focuses on meeting pointing goals and minimizing the need to desaturate the reaction wheel. The use of planning allows for intelligent use of the reaction wheel and accommodates time-changing goals and orbit-varying magnetic fields. Preliminary results show trajectories with fractional-degree-accuracy, as well as management of reaction wheel momentum and avoidance of stiction. We also compare to a magnetorquer-only planning-based control system and show better convergence and faster slews.
papers.title_ja: 磁気姿勢制御と単一リアクションホイールを備えた衛星のための軌道計画姿勢制御システム
papers.summary_ja: 低軌道衛星において、リアクションホイールとマグネトーキューアのトレードオフを解決するため、単一リアクションホイールと3本のマグネトーキューアを用いたハイブリッド姿勢制御システムを提案する。軌道計画制御手法により、指向目標の達成とリアクションホイールのデサチュレーション（飽和解除）の最小化を同時に実現する。この手法は、時間変化する目標や軌道に伴う磁界の変化に適応し、分数度精度の軌道生成とスティクション回避を可能にする。マグネトーキューアのみを用いた計画ベース制御と比較し、収束性とスlew速度の向上を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: 軌道力学・姿勢制御・計画ベース最適化の組み合わせであり、ユーザーの関心領域に直結する。

papers.title: Accuracy is not compatibility: two Evo 2 checkpoints hinge on one FP8 matrix multiplication
papers.summary: FP8 formats specify how values are stored, not how products are summed; this gap can break checkpoints. Evo 2, a DNA language model, documents a Hopper FP8 requirement for its 1B and 40B checkpoints. On two Blackwell (sm_120) GPUs both fail the developers' forward test (the 7B passes); on an RTX 5070 Ti the 40B's next-base accuracy is 25.7%, near guessing. Greater accuracy breaks them, as BioNeMo saw for the 40B on Hopper: natively, 99.996% of one projection's outputs are correctly rounded (H100: about 30%), and fp32 accumulation of the same operands fails. Our H100 FP8 GEMM emulator, mmaemu (bit-exact on captured 1B projections), localises the dependence to the 1B's first projection (of 21), where exact sums fail but pass when shrunk by the H100's 1.4% (measured in-sample), not 2.1%. The 40B fails with only its first projection native. Emulating only that projection, weights unchanged, raises 40B BRCA1 variant-classification AUROC from 0.434 to 0.869 (H100: 0.868) on the RTX 5070 Ti, despite a narrow forward-test miss, and 0.481 to 0.867 on an RTX PRO 6000. We tested one model family but not training origin; releases should specify reference arithmetic.
papers.title_ja: 精度は互換性を意味しない：Evo 2 の2つのチェックポイントは1つのFP8行列積に依存している
papers.summary_ja: DNA言語モデルEvo 2のチェックポイントが、GPUアーキテクチャ間のFP8行列積（GEMM）の微小な数値差により互換性を失う問題を報告する。Blackwell GPUでは精度向上によりチェックポイントが破綻する一方、Hopper GPUでは特定の射影層の丸め誤差がモデル性能に決定的な影響を与えることを示した。開発者はビット単位の正確なエミュレータを用いて、この依存性を特定し、単一の射影層の演算をエミュレートするだけで、変異分類のAUROCを0.434から0.869まで回復させることを実証した。モデルリリース時には参照算術の明示が不可欠であると提言している。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの量子化・推論環境依存性と実務的な評価手法に直結

papers.title: Residual-based Adaptive Refinement of hp-Variational PINNs for elliptic PDEs with geometric singularities and localized features
papers.summary: Physics-Informed Neural Networks approximate the solution of boundary value problems by minimizing the strong-form residual, their accuracy is often limited near corner and crack singularities, sharp layers and localized features and the enforcement of Neumann boundary conditions remains challenging. In hp-Variational Physics-Informed Neural Networks, the problem is formulated in a Petrov-Galerkin weak form, reducing the differentiation order applied to the neural network, while boundary constraints are imposed through penalty terms. The variational residual is evaluated using fixed Gauss quadrature points and the strong-form residual on a fixed collocation set, which may fail to capture regions of rapid variation. To address this issue, we integrate hp-Variational Physics-Informed Neural Networks with Residual-based Adaptive Refinement. During training, the strong-form residual is computed on a dense candidate pool and points with the largest residuals are added adaptively to the collocation set. Since the weak formulation is defined in $H^{1}(\Omega)$, it avoids the $H^{2}(\Omega)$ regularity requirement that fails on cracked and non-convex domains. The proposed method is validated on four two-dimensional elliptic problems and consistently achieves substantial reductions in relative $L^{2}$, absolute $L^{\infty}$ and relative $H^{1}$ semi-norm errors through adaptive residual-driven point placement.
papers.title_ja: 幾何学的特異点と局所的特徴を持つ楕円型偏微分方程式に対する、残差ベース適応的細分化を用いたhp変分PINN
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）の精度向上を目的とし、hp変分形式と残差ベースの適応的細分化手法を統合した新しいアプローチを提案する。従来の固定配置点では捉えきれない急峻な変化や特異点付近の誤差を低減するため、学習過程で残差が大きい点を動的に追加する仕組みを導入した。この手法は、非凸領域やクラックを含む問題におけるH^2正則性の要件を回避しつつ、境界条件の強制も安定して行える。2次元楕円型問題4種での検証により、L2ノルムやH1半ノルムなどの誤差が大幅に低減することが示された。
papers.relevance_reason: PINNと適応的メッシュ細分化の組み合わせは、サロゲートモデルの精度向上に直結する重要手法であるため。

papers.title: FORGE: Feasible Online Reduced-Order Reference Generation and Whole-Body Execution for Agile Humanoid Locomotion
papers.summary: This paper presents a two-stage learning framework for versatile and agile humanoid locomotion that couples online reduced-order model (ROM) reference generation with whole-body tracking control. In the first stage, we train a command-conditioned whole-body reference generator using single rigid body dynamics combined with full humanoid kinematics. In the second stage, the frozen ROM policy is rolled out online to generate references for training a whole-body tracking policy on the full-order dynamics model. Learning a kino-dynamically consistent reference generator in the simplified ROM space enables us to generate references over a broad command space and over multiple locomotion strategies using a single unified framework. We demonstrate the approach on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot, achieving longitudinal velocities from -2.0 m/s to 2.8 m/s, lateral velocities up to +-1.0 m/s, angular velocities up to +-3.0 rad/s, one-legged hopping, and continuous transitions across the commands, all using one unified reference policy and one whole-body tracking policy.
papers.title_ja: FORGE: 俊敏なヒューマノイド歩行のための実行可能なオンライン縮約モデル参照生成と全身実行
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、ヒューマノイドロボットの俊敏な歩行を実現する2段階の学習フレームワークを提案する。第1段階では、単一剛体力学と完全な運動学を組み合わせた縮約モデル（ROM）空間で、コマンド条件付きの全身参照生成器を訓練する。第2段階では、凍結されたROMポリシーをオンラインでロールアウトし、その参照に基づいて完全な力学モデル上で全身追従ポリシーを訓練する。このアプローチにより、Unitree G1ロボット上で単一の統合ポリシーを用いて、幅広い速度や姿勢変化、片足ジャンプなどの多様な動作を連続的に実現した。
papers.relevance_reason: 縮約モデルと強化学習による制御設計が関心に合致

papers.title: Machine learning-guided real-time AC optimal transmission switching
papers.summary: The operation of power grids has substantial economic consequences, affecting generation costs and, ultimately, electricity prices. The Optimal Transmission Switching (OTS) problem seeks to reduce these costs by selectively switching off transmission lines. However, OTS gives rise to a challenging mixed-integer nonlinear optimization problem that is difficult to solve at operationally relevant timescales, particularly as rapidly changing loads create a need for real-time switching decisions. To address this challenge, we develop a machine learning-guided method that identifies high quality line switching decisions in real time. Specifically, we construct a grid-specific switching-value model that rapidly estimates the generation-cost reduction associated with opening transmission lines by fine-tuning a pretrained model for AC optimal power flow (AC-OPF). The switching-value model provides signals to guide promising switching decisions, and topologies proposed by the model are evaluated using exact AC-OPF solvers to verify feasibility and obtain the actual generation cost. We develop multiple strategies that use the ML surrogate to efficiently explore the combinatorial space of transmission topologies, including Fixed-Rank Search, Adaptive-Rank Search, and Swap-Enhanced Search. Across multiple benchmark networks, our proposed algorithms identify line switching decisions that significantly reduce generation cost within a 50s computational budget. In particular, under a realistic data center buildout scenario on the 2,000-bus synthetic Texas grid, our approach reduces generation costs by 31.97% and gross nodal load payments by 94.34%. More broadly, our results demonstrate that a fine-tuned surrogate can effectively guide search even without guaranteeing feasibility, enabling classical optimization methods to tackle large nonlinear combinatorial problems on operationally relevant timescales.
papers.title_ja: 機械学習によるリアルタイムAC最適送電切替
papers.summary_ja: 電力網の最適送電切替（OTS）問題において、計算コストの高い混合整数非線形最適化をリアルタイムで解決するための手法を提案する。事前学習済みAC-OPFモデルをファインチューニングしたサロゲートモデルを用い、送電線の開閉によるコスト削減効果を高速に推定する。この推定値をシグナルとして活用し、Fixed-Rank Searchなどの戦略で組合せ空間を効率的に探索する。2,000バス網のシナリオにおいて、50秒の計算予算内で発電コストを約32%削減する成果を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデルによる組合せ最適化の高速化という手法が関心に合致

papers.title: Variational Consequence-Driven Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) typically mitigates distribution shift by imposing divergence constraints on the action distributions of the learned and behavior policies. However, this paradigm cannot ensure the underlying dynamic consistency structure: even minor action deviations can lead to drastically different transitions, inadvertently driving the agent away from the offline dataset. To address this, we explore policy constraints through their induced state-consequence distributions rather than relying on pure action-distribution matching. Nevertheless, directly enforcing such consequence-aware constraints is computationally intractable without access to the true underlying dynamics model. To bypass this issue, we propose Structural Behavior Regularization (StBR), which replaces the intractable objective with a closed-form latent divergence. Structuring this latent space to reflect transition dynamics renders the latent divergence a theoretically bounded surrogate for the true consequence-distribution divergence. By regularizing the learned policy with this latent divergence, StBR adaptively tightens the behavior constraint in dynamics-sensitive regions, effectively preventing deviations outside the offline dataset. Empirically, we demonstrate that StBR achieves superior performance across diverse offline RL benchmarks.
papers.title_ja: 変分・結果駆動型オフライン強化学習
papers.summary_ja: オフライン強化学習において、行動分布の一致だけでは状態遷移の動的構造を維持できず、データ分布外へ逸脱する問題を解決する手法を提案する。真のダイナミクスモデルに依存せず、潜在空間における閉形式の発散を用いて結果分布の制約を近似する「Structural Behavior Regularization (StBR)」を導入する。この手法は、動的に敏感な領域で行動制約を適応的に強化し、オフラインデータセットからの逸脱を効果的に防止する。多様なオフライン強化学習ベンチマークにおいて、既存手法を上回る性能を実証している。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習の手法全般に関心があり、オフラインRLの改善は直接関連する。

papers.title: Regional accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for recirculation in a deep lid-driven cavity
papers.summary: Deep lid-driven cavities contain strong motion beneath the lid and much weaker recirculation at depth, so agreement in bulk velocity is an incomplete assessment of a computed flow. We examine data-free physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for steady, two-dimensional incompressible flow in a cavity of depth-to-width ratio five at Reynolds numbers 100, 250, 500 and 1000. An established hard-constrained streamfunction formulation is combined with prescribed regional collocation, transferred initialization, and selected residual-scaling and envelope variants. Independent spectral/$hp$ calculations with the same Gaussian-regularized lid provide the reference fields. For a cavity of depth-to-width ratio $D/W=5$ at Reynolds numbers $\mathrm{Re}=100$, 250, 500, and 1000, evaluation on a common $121\times605$ grid gives interior relative velocity discrepancies of 5.130\%--7.850\%. Over the same cases, floor-region relative velocity discrepancies remain below 5\%, with absolute RMS discrepancies ranging from $1.255\times10^{-10}U$ to $2.332\times10^{-9}U$, where $U$ is the lid-velocity scale. In a separate $161\times801$ assessment at $\Rey=1000$, the refined workflow lowers interior velocity discrepancy from 5.624\% to 2.658\% and gauge-aligned pressure RMS discrepancy from $2.793\times10^{-3}$ to $1.167\times10^{-3}\rho U^2$. The improvements compare accumulated training workflows and do not isolate regional sampling. Configuration rankings depend on both region and observable. These finite-budget comparisons establish where the retained workflows agree with the reference and where rotational-field discrepancies remain substantial.
papers.title_ja: 深いリッド駆動キャビティにおける再循環に対する物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINNs）の局所精度
papers.summary_ja: 深いリッド駆動キャビティ内の定常2次元不可圧流に対して、データフリーな物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）の局所精度を評価した。硬制約付きストリーム関数定式化と、指定された領域でのコロケーション、初期化の転移、残差スケーリングなどの手法を組み合わせ、Reynolds数100〜1000の範囲で検証した。スペクトル法による参照解と比較し、内部領域の相対速度誤差は5.130%〜7.850%、床面付近では5%未満であることを示した。さらに改良ワークフローにより、内部速度誤差を2.658%まで低減し、圧力誤差も大幅に改善した。本研究は、PINNが全体平均ではなく局所的な流場特性を捉える際の限界と改善可能性を定量的に明らかにしている。

papers.title: Inherent Failure Modes of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Buoyancy-Driven Flow: Role of Non-Dimensionalization in Network Training
papers.summary: We investigate the influence of non-dimensionalization on the trainability and accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for buoyancy-driven flows. Using a differentially heated square cavity at $\mathrm{Pr}=0.71$ and $\mathrm{Ra}=10^3$--$10^5$, we compare thermal-diffusive and free-fall velocity scalings under identical training conditions. The free-fall scaling, with a unit buoyancy coefficient, achieves errors below 1.1\% in the mean Nusselt number for $\mathrm{Ra}\le10^4$, whereas the diffusive scaling, with a buoyancy coefficient of $\mathrm{Ra}\,\mathrm{Pr}$, produces errors of 157--650\% and diverges at $\mathrm{Ra}=10^5$. We identify a coefficient-induced gradient imbalance, with the dominant buoyancy-related contribution to the loss gradient scaling as $(\mathrm{Ra}\,\mathrm{Pr})^2$, and confirm it through direct gradient measurements. Neither sparse-data supervision nor adaptive loss weighting resolves the training difficulties under the tested conditions. For unsteady convection, the free-fall PINN accurately predicts long-time heat transfer but fails to capture the transient Nusselt-number overshoot. These findings establish non-dimensionalization as an important design consideration for improving PINN trainability in buoyancy-driven flows.
papers.title_ja: 浮力駆動流れにおける物理情報ニューラルネットワークの固有の失敗モード：ネットワーク学習における無次元化の役割
papers.summary_ja: 浮力駆動流れにおける物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）の学習可能性と精度への無次元化の影響を調査した。自由落下速度スケーリングを用いるとレイノルズ数10^4以下で平均ヌセルト数の誤差が1.1%未満となる一方、拡散スケーリングでは誤差が157〜650%に達し、高レイノルズ数では発散する。損失勾配における浮力項の寄与が(Ra*Pr)^2でスケールする勾配不均衡が原因として特定された。スパースデータや適応的損失重み付けでは解決できず、非定常対流では過渡的なヌセルト数オーバーシュートを捕捉できない限界も示された。

papers.title: Optimization-based lane-changing trajectory planning in mixed traffic with embedded input convex neural networks
papers.summary: Lane-changing (LC) maneuvers are highly challenging vehicle interactions, with substantial implications for traffic safety and efficiency. Developing effective LC strategies for connected and automated vehicles in mixed traffic is complicated by the uncertainty associated with surrounding-vehicle behavior and the computational burden of embedding realistic prediction models within optimization schemes. To capture these complex interactions while retaining tractability, this study proposes a data-driven optimization framework that embeds neural network (NN) surrogates for safety and lateral comfort within a B\'ezier-curve-based trajectory planner. Specifically, the safety cost during the LC process is quantified via a surrogate composed of an input convex recurrent neural network (ICRNN) encoding the planned trajectory, a fully input convex neural network (FICNN) embedding the LC duration, and a partially input convex neural network (PICNN) decoder fusing them with historical traffic states; separately, another FICNN surrogate approximates the optimal lateral comfort cost as a function of the LC duration. Both surrogates are embedded via linear programming (LP) formulations, avoiding the binary variables required by conventional mixed-integer programming (MIP) approaches for NN-embedded optimization. We further theoretically establish their exactness at optimality and extend the framework to problems with additional analytical objective terms and multiple surrogates. Experiments on a hybrid dataset combining real-world and simulated trajectories demonstrate that the proposed method achieves surrogate accuracy competitive with unconstrained baselines while substantially improving optimization efficiency over conventional MIPs. Closed-loop simulations further show that the proposed planners markedly reduce the weighted planning cost and consistently outperform baseline methods.
papers.title_ja: 埋め込み型入力凸ニューラルネットワークを用いた混在交通における最適化ベースの車線変更軌道計画
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、混在交通環境における自動車の車線変更軌道計画において、安全性と横向き快適性のコストをニューラルネットワーク（NN）サロゲートモデルで近似する手法を提案する。入力凸NN（ICRNN, FICNN, PICNN）を用いることで、従来の混合整数計画（MIP）に必要だった二値変数を回避し、線形計画（LP）として定式化可能にする。理論的に最適解の正確性を保証し、実データとシミュレーションデータのハイブリッドセットを用いた実験では、従来のMIP手法と比較して計算効率を大幅に向上させつつ、同等以上の精度と計画コストの低減を実証した。

papers.title: Agentic AI Reasoning and Learned Sampling for Task-Aware Projection Selection in Sparse-View CT: Predicting Hemodynamics
papers.summary: Sparse-view computed tomography (CT) reduces the number of acquired projections, but conventional sampling strategies are designed primarily for image reconstruction rather than for downstream physical inference. Here, we investigate optimal task-aware projection selection for directly predicting hemodynamics from sparse CT angiography (CTA) measurements. Using computational fluid dynamics simulations of intracranial aneurysms, we generate synthetic fan-beam CTA projections and train a Fourier neural operator (FNO) to predict two targets: the spatially resolved time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS) field and the spatially averaged TAWSS. The FNO was coupled with optimal input selection for simultaneous optimal sampling and training. Our goal was to investigate if agentic AI could discover optimal sampling strategies that outperform current methods. We compared fixed uniform and golden-angle sampling with three task-aware optimal selection strategies: Gumbel-Softmax, a Soft top-K method, and an agentic AI selector. The methods were compared at different view selection budgets. A detailed analysis of the AI agent was performed to understand its reasoning and performance. For spatially resolved TAWSS, Agentic and Soft top-K achieve the lowest mean errors (Agentic performs slightly better) and substantially outperform fixed sampling under extreme sparsity. For spatially averaged TAWSS, optimized selection becomes important at extremely sparse acquisitions. Analysis of the selected masks reveals multiple distinct subsets concentrated around informative regions. Moreover, masks optimized for hemodynamic prediction yield poor image reconstructions, showing that task-optimal acquisition differs fundamentally from reconstruction-optimal acquisition. This work suggests the possibility of designing sparse acquisitions directly around downstream physical quantities.
papers.title_ja: スパースビューCTにおけるタスク認識型投影選択のためのエージェント型AI推論と学習済みサンプリング：血流動態の予測
papers.summary_ja: スパースビューCTから血流動態を直接予測する際、画像再構成ではなく下流タスク（血流動態）に最適化された投影選択戦略を提案する。Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) を用い、Gumbel-Softmax やエージェント型AIによる最適選択手法を比較評価した。結果、極端なスパース条件下でエージェント型AIが固定サンプリングを大きく上回り、タスク最適化と再構成最適化が根本的に異なることを示した。

papers.title: Exponential-Nemytskii Neural Operators: Learning Field Evolution Across Step Sizes
papers.summary: In variable-step operator learning, agreement at observed step sizes does not by itself determine predictions at other temporal resolutions. We propose an operator whose step-size dependence is prescribed by a first-order Duhamel approximation of semilinear dynamics. It combines exact linear propagation with a local nonlinear function of the field and its derivatives, allowing evaluation below the observation interval without supervision densely sampled across step sizes. Under suitable conditions and at fixed spatial resolution, we prove that agreement between models at two step sizes controls their prediction differences throughout a prescribed range. We also give conditions for local identifiability of both components from two step sizes, supporting interpretation of the learned structure. A latent extension applies the same construction to learned fields. We evaluate the base model on two synthetic problems and the extension on two real datasets against several baselines.
papers.title_ja: 指数型Nemytskiiニューラルオペレータ：ステップサイズをまたぐ場の進化の学習

papers.title: Learning Kolmogorov Backward Operators for Spectral Analysis and Forecasting: A Data-Driven Variational Galerkin Framework
papers.summary: For a time-homogeneous Markov process, the fixed-lag solution operator \( (T_\tau f)(x)=\mathbb E[f(X_{t+\tau})\mid X_t=x] \) of the Kolmogorov backward equation evolves observables linearly and deterministically, even when the dynamics are stochastic. We approximate this operator using a two-stage method where we first approximate this operator directly from data, without knowledge of the governing equation (e.g., Fourier Neural Operator), and then compress the Galerkin projection onto a finite-dimensional observable space that is fixed in advance or selected variationally. The error analysis traces the learning error of the estimator, the sampling error of the Galerkin inner products, and the invariance and reconstruction properties of the observable space to the computed spectra and forecasts. The sampling error enters only through a multiplicative factor. Near an isolated spectral cluster, the invariance defect of a subspace controls its distance from the target invariant subspace. The forecast error is controlled by the one-step error of the reduced model and the projection error of the observable; when the measure is invariant and the reduced model preserves constants and is stable on mean-zero observables, the bound is uniform in the horizon. For deterministic dynamics, a learning rate for Fourier neural operators (FNOs) gives one explicit bound for the learning error. Numerical experiments illustrate spectral approximation and forecasting, including long-rollout stability and a comparison with extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) when fewer transition pairs than basis functions are observed.
papers.title_ja: スペクトル解析と予測のためのコルモゴロフ後方演算子の学習：データ駆動型変分ガレルキン枠組み
papers.summary_ja: 時齐一マルコフ過程のコルモゴロフ後方方程式の解演算子を、支配方程式の知識なしにデータから直接近似する2段階手法を提案する。まずFourier Neural Operator (FNO) により演算子を学習し、次に有限次元の観測量空間へのガレルキン射影を圧縮する。誤差解析により、学習誤差・サンプリング誤差・観測量空間の不変性がスペクトルと予測誤差に与える影響を定量化し、特に不変測度下では予測誤差が予測期間に依存しない一様境界を示す。数値実験では、長期間ロールアウトの安定性と、EDMDとの比較を通じて、少ない遷移データでも高精度なスペクトル近似と予測が可能であることを示した。

papers.title: Surrogate Uncertainty for Black-box Visual Grounding
papers.summary: Visual grounding is crucial for robots to understand language instructions with visual observations. This paper addresses the problem of visual grounding uncertainties, where a robot uses a black-box vision-language model (VLM) to ground free-form natural-language instructions to target objects. Prevailing methods derive uncertainty from the VLM itself. Yet, outputs of the VLM, e.g., generated uncertainties, are from the same parameters and structures producing the predictions, and inherit the bias. We give a formal Bayesian definition of the problem that treats the VLM prediction as an observation. An external surrogate Bayesian model then quantifies per-query uncertainty over a local neighborhood of a held-out calibration set, decomposed into aleatoric and epistemic components. A hierarchical retrieval across input modalities realizes a compact joint-space neighborhood, mitigating the curse of dimensionality. The estimator further integrates with conformal prediction or model-based planning for active visual grounding, where robots are allowed to take verbal or physical actions to ground targets. Across grounding benchmarks and state-of-the-art VLMs, it consistently improves both calibration and task performance. On a real Fetch robot under open-world instructions, it enables principled trade-offs between confident action and information gathering, substantially improving robustness.
papers.title_ja: ブラックボックス視覚グラウンディングにおけるサロゲート不確実性
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、ロボットがブラックボックスの視覚言語モデル（VLM）を用いた視覚グラウンディングにおける不確実性定量化手法を提案する。VLM自体の出力バイアスを回避するため、予測を観測値として扱い、外部のベイズサロゲートモデルで不確実性を推定する。階層的検索により高次元空間の近傍を効率的に特定し、アレイティックとエピステミックな不確実性を分解する。この推定器は整合性予測やモデルベース計画と統合可能で、実ロボット環境における頑健性と行動の信頼性向上に寄与する。

papers.title: A physics-informed uncertainty-aware surrogate for $p$-$n$ junction diodes
papers.summary: We develop an uncertainty-aware physics-informed surrogate for a one-dimensional $p$-$n$ junction diode, conditioned on device length, doping and bias. Using the internal state of the device as predicted by the surrogate we develop a test-suite of quantities of interest including the terminal current, depletion width, peak field and stored charge. The formalism and the quantities are can be extended to asymmetric junction and two-dimensional diodes as shown by means of benchmark analysis. For the one-dimensional symmetric junction surrogate, we obtain 0.11% median $L_1$ error on the electrostatic potential, and 1.5% and 0.61% on the electron and hole densities. Finally, we develop an uncertainty analysis which determines the validity of surrogate answer within the user-specified tolerance.

papers.title: NEOPIC: A Neural Operator Framework for Particle-based Kinetic Plasma Simulations
papers.summary: We introduce NEOPIC, a framework for learning the field operator in particle-based methods applied to kinetic plasma simulations. Its key novelty is a neural operator that acts directly on the empirical measure of the particles, rather than on a grid, and is evaluated at the particle positions. No mesh or tree is needed and, unlike grid-based neural operators, no deposition onto a mesh takes place, so the particle noise that dominates the inputs of particle simulations is not aliased. Since it replaces only the field solve, it serves as a plug-and-play field solver for particle-based methods: it can be trained on data from particle-in-cell, particle-in-Fourier or tree codes, and combined with any time integrator, including implicit schemes. We prove that the discrete evaluation coincides with the continuous operator at any number of particles (representation equivalence) and derive an error analysis that separates sampling, learning and time-stepping errors: up to the learning error, NEOPIC has the error structure of standard Monte Carlo particle methods. We show that the particle noise in the training data acts as an implicit regularizer, which gives guidance on the number of training particles in relation to the particle numbers used at inference. A complexity analysis shows that NEOPIC is an $O(N_p)$ method whose constants are set by the architecture alone, independently of any mesh or tree. Numerical experiments on electrostatic benchmarks in two and three dimensions, including Landau damping, two-stream and bump-on-tail instabilities, a cyclotron mini-app and a Penning trap, confirm the theoretical findings. A single model trained on several mini-apps generated by different reference methods captures all of them and remains stable up to twice the training time window, which points towards foundation models for fields in particle-based methods.
papers.title_ja: NEOPIC: 粒子ベースの動論プラズマシミュレーションのためのニューラルオペレータフレームワーク
papers.summary_ja: 粒子ベースの動論プラズマシミュレーションにおいて、メッシュやツリー構造を必要とせずに粒子の経験分布に直接作用するニューラルオペレータを提案する。従来のグリッドベース手法と異なり、粒子ノイズのエイリアシングを回避し、フィールドソルバーとしてプラグアンドプレイで統合可能である。理論的に離散評価と連続オペレータの等価性を証明し、サンプリング・学習・時間ステップ誤差を分離した誤差解析を行う。2次元・3次元の電磁気ベンチマーク実験により、異なる参照手法で生成されたデータから学習した単一モデルが安定して動作することを示し、粒子ベース手法における「ファウンデーションモデル」の可能性を提示する。

papers.title: Practical Assessment of Agentic Systems in Acoustics
papers.summary: In engineering, applications of artificial intelligence have so far been largely limited to surrogate models and optimization tasks. Large language models changed this, as they can write software from a task given in words. Placed inside a harness, a system of components that lets it search for information and execute software, such a model becomes an agent that can take over recurring engineering tasks. This work measures how the model and the elements of the harness shape the performance and behavior of the agent in two common acoustic applications. In the first, the agent detects and locates faults in audio recordings from a vehicle interior with near-perfect accuracy. A benchmark on this task shows that a weak model sets a limit that no harness design can overcome, and that design choices take effect only once the model is capable enough to use them. In the second, a case study on the design of a metamaterial unit cell, the agent reliably finds designs that achieve a specified insertion loss over a given frequency range. The results aim to help the reader understand what each element of an agent contributes and how to design an agent for acoustic tasks.
papers.title_ja: 音響学におけるエージェント型システムの実用的評価

papers.title: Exposure Is Not Commitment: Double-Stratified Evaluation of Latent Monitors for Tool-Using Agents
papers.summary: Tool-using language agents are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection, and a growing literature probes model internals to catch unsafe actions before they execute, with sharply conflicting results. We argue much of the conflict is an evaluation artifact, and propose a double-stratification protocol: separate injection exposure from behavioral commitment, in both the evaluation and the training population. On the primary Qwen AgentDojo grid, monitors trained on the naive mixed unsafe-versus-rest contrast mostly learn exposure: they flag exposed trajectories whether or not the agent complies, and barely predict which cases turn unsafe. Retrained on exposed cases only, the same probe families predict the model's own unsafe tool call up to two steps early, the maximum the three-step trajectories admit (logistic AUROC 0.853, matched by a trained TF-IDF text baseline at 0.855). Mistral-7B reaches 0.896 and OLMo-2-7B 0.912; their naive contrasts learn different things: inverted exposure ranking on one, both axes on the other. Representations separate on exposure (probe 1.000 versus trained text 0.908) and where visible context is sanitized or unavailable. Training contrast alone reproduces the shape of recent pre-action-probe negative results, one candidate explanation for the conflict: the signal exists, but the model's own zero-shot forecast and NLA verbalizations do not reliably recover it. An unstratified AUROC overstates what a latent monitor knows, and what a naive contrast learns is population-dependent: evaluations should stratify both.
papers.title_ja: 露出はコミットメントではない：ツール使用エージェントの潜在モニターに対する二重層別評価

papers.title: Artifact Distillation: Training-Free Transfer from Frontier to Small Language Models
papers.summary: Closing the gap between frontier and smaller language models is usually approached by distillation: fine-tuning the small model (student) on a frontier model's (teacher) outputs, which binds transfer to training compute and leaves the transferred knowledge largely opaque. We propose Artifact Distillation: a teacher solves training instances and externalizes its problem-solving procedure into an artifact bank that a student queries at inference time, with no gradient updates. Across four LiveBench tasks, a bank written by Claude Opus 4.5 lets Claude Haiku 4.5 outperform unaided Claude Sonnet 4.5 on spatial reasoning (0.707 vs. 0.647) at 60% of its cost, and reach Sonnet 4.5's level on table joining at 89% of its cost. The same raw bank raises Qwen3.5-27B's pooled score from 0.730 to 0.800, showing that transfer is not confined to the teacher's model family.
papers.title_ja: アーティファクト蒸留：フロンティアモデルから小型言語モデルへの学習不要な知識移転
papers.summary_ja: フロンティアLLMの推論プロセスを「アーティファクトバンク」として外部化し、小型モデルが推論時にこれを参照することで、グラデーション更新なしに性能を向上させる手法を提案する。Claude Opus 4.5が作成したバンクにより、Claude Haiku 4.5は空間推論タスクでSonnet 4.5を上回り、コスト効率も大幅に改善した。また、Qwen3.5-27Bでも同様の効果が見られ、モデルファミリーを跨いだ知識移転の汎用性を示した。
